symptom: `alter workflow M.W { drop aiAgentTask1 outcome '' }` (and the old `drop condition '' on X`) deleted the activity's default outcome and printed "Altered workflow"; on a parallel split the same statement deleted the first path. Measured on TestApp's Studio Pro-authored workflow.Workflow1 (aiAgentTask1 Outcomes 2 -> 1 items)
cause: DropOutcome/DropBranch (wfmutator and the MCP mutator) compared the address with DGetString(Value) / a lenient JSON unmarshal, which read an outcome that stores NO string value (ParallelSplitOutcome, VoidConditionOutcome, BooleanConditionOutcome) as "", so an empty value matched the first valueless member
fix: a value address matches only an outcome whose Value is a stored string (wfmutator: type assertion on DGet; mcp: pedOutcomeElem.hasValue requires a JSON string); 'Default' still names a void outcome by type
insight: The #791 review claimed value-addressed drops cannot land on another kind's member; they can when the accessor maps 'absent' to the zero value. Any match of an author-supplied string against a getter that returns "" for missing is an address that silently hits the first member lacking the field
